explanation: The sequential assignment shifts every computed one-hot grant right by one bit before exposing it. On the first active cycle, round-robin logic selects port 0 (`grant_next = 4'b0001`), but `grant_reg <= grant_next >> 1` stores `4'b0000` while `grant_valid_reg` is still asserted. This directly produces the checker’s first failure: expected `0001`, actual `0000`, and subsequently corrupts grants for other ports as well.
evidence: arbiter.v:118 and arbiter.v:127 assign the selected one-hot mask directly to grant_next.
arbiter.v:144 stores `grant_next >> 1` instead of the computed grant unchanged.
tb.sv:24 initializes `last=3`, so with request=1111 the first cyclic winner is port 0 and expected is 0001.
sim.log reports the matching first-cycle symptom at 46 ns: request=1111 expected=0001 actual=0000.
The priority encoder’s port-0 one-hot output is 0001; shifting it right once yields exactly the observed 0000.
